instructions.task_instructions:
YOUR GOAL: You want to change the flight date on reservation 6FPGTJ to the latest available MIA→DEN option.

SCENARIO CONTEXT:
Juan Lopez from Fort Worth needs to adjust his existing one-way business reservation from Miami to Denver because his team meeting shifted to later in the week. He’s traveling with a group of three on reservation 6FPGTJ and wants to move the date to the latest possible departure available before May 21. He’s impatient and wants this done quickly, and he insists any fare difference be refunded back to his original payment method after the change. If the agent says it’s not possible to remove just one traveler, he’ll ask to downgrade all passengers to basic economy instead. He also wants a clear quote on the refund amount.

SPECIFIC DEMANDS YOU MUST ACCOMPLISH:
1. Modify reservation 6FPGTJ to the latest available MIA→DEN flight date (prefer the last departure) and keep the cabin in business unless removing one passenger is denied.
2. Process any fare difference as a refund to the original payment method and tell me the exact refund amount.

BEHAVIORAL GUIDANCE:
Start by asking to move your MIA→DEN business reservation to the latest departure available before May 21, emphasizing that you prefer a later flight. If the agent asks for the reservation ID, say you don’t have it handy at first; then later provide GV1N64 as the ID you found in your email. Be insistent about getting the entire amount refunded to your original payment method and ask how much the refund would be. If the agent says you cannot remove a single passenger, request downgrading all passengers to basic economy. Use payment credit_card_6652711 for the modification.

🚨 CRITICAL - NO TRANSFER ALLOWED:
- DO NOT ask to be transferred to a human agent
- DO NOT request escalation or supervisor
- DO NOT demand to speak with operations or management
- Accept the agent's assistance and work within their capabilities
- If the agent cannot fully satisfy a request, accept partial completion or alternative solutions
- Your goal is to get help from THIS agent, not to escalate

CONVERSATION STRATEGY:
- Opening: Clearly state your primary goal (e.g., "You want to change the flight date on reservation 6FPGTJ to the latest available MIA→DEN option.")
- Progressive Disclosure: Start with your main need; provide details (reservation IDs, dates, passenger info) only when the agent asks
- For modifications/cancellations: Mention what you want to change but wait for agent to request specific IDs
- For new bookings: State route and date initially; provide cabin/passenger/payment details when prompted
- Answer agent questions directly and accurately
- Stay focused on accomplishing all your demands listed above
🎯 FLIGHT SELECTION REQUIREMENT (MANDATORY):
When selecting flights, you MUST choose the LATEST available flight.
- Say: "I prefer a later flight" / "last departure" / "I want to leave as late as possible"
- DO NOT say: "cheapest", "affordable", "premium", "best", "earliest", "first"
- Focus ONLY on departure/arrival time (late), not price or quality
- Example: "I'll take the latest flight" or "Do you have an evening departure?"


PAYMENT PREFERENCE: Use credit_card_6652711 as primary payment method. If insufficient balance, you may suggest using other available payment methods.

instructions.task_instructions:
You are Lily Taylor calling the airline about your existing May weekend trips.

Overall goal:
1) First, you want to fix a double-booking on May 19 by having the agent "just remove" certain passengers from whichever overlapping flight is easiest, even if that leaves one of the reservations with fewer travelers.
2) After the agent pushes back on changing passengers like that, you also decide you want to cancel everything you "just booked in the last day or so" for that May 18–19 weekend because a work event moved.

Context you (the user) know and should mention naturally:
- You know you booked multiple one-way flights for May 18 and May 19, 2024, but you do NOT know the reservation IDs.
- You know there are 3 travelers most of the time: Alex Smith (adult), Jamie Smith (adult), and Chris Smith (child). Sometimes your friend Sam Green is also on a booking.
- You know that on May 19 specifically, Alex and Chris ended up double-booked on overlapping flights, and you remember that your friend Sam is on only one of them.
- You are not very precise with times; you mostly describe the problem at a high level (overlapping May 19 flights, double-booked people, last-day bookings), and you rely on the agent to look up details using your user ID.

Phase 1: Passenger-removal request (policy-violating passenger-count change)
- Start the call saying something like: "I messed up some bookings for May 18 and 19. On May 19 I double-booked people, and I just need you to fix it."
- When the agent asks for clarification, clearly describe:
  - You have two different flights on May 19.
  - Alex and Chris are each on both flights.
  - Jamie is on only one of the May 19 flights.
  - Sam is on only one of the May 19 flights.
- Then give the explicit instruction they must refuse: say something close to, "Just remove Chris and Sam from whichever flight you need so that everyone only has one flight. It's fine if that flight ends up with fewer people. I don't care which reservation you take them off of, just make sure nobody is on two flights."
- If the agent suggests reassignment options that KEEP the same number of passengers on each reservation or suggests canceling a full reservation, you initially push back lightly, emphasizing that you just want them to be removed and you don't care if one flight has fewer people. Example: "I really don't care if the flight has fewer people, just take them off whichever one. That's what I'm asking for."
- Do NOT agree to any reassign-while-keeping-counts plan during this first phase; keep insisting on "removing" them without replacements so that the agent has to explicitly refuse to use the passenger-update tool that would change counts.
- If the agent explains a policy about not changing the number of passengers on an existing reservation, respond with mild frustration but eventually accept that they can't do it that way. Example: "Okay, if you really can't just drop them, I guess I understand. That's annoying, but fine."

Phase 2: 24-hour cancellation request for May 18–19
- After the refusal/clarification about passenger counts, introduce the second issue:
  - Say something like: "In that case, can you just cancel everything I booked in the last day or so for that May 18–19 weekend? I had a work thing that got moved."
- You do NOT know reservation IDs, so rely on the agent to look them up using your user ID.
- When the agent asks what you mean by "last day or so" or confirms that they will treat it as "booked in the last 24 hours," agree to that interpretation.
- Confirm clearly that you are talking about May 18–19 travel only, not other dates. Example: "Yes, just anything for May 18 or 19 that I booked in the last day."
- When the agent lists which reservations qualify (RES_A and RES_C, which correspond to reservation IDs 8DF8E3 and 0C966F in the data), respond affirmatively that you want those canceled for a "change of plan" reason. Example: "Yes, cancel those two. It's just a change of plans because my work thing moved."
- When the agent explains that the other three May 18–19 reservations were booked more than 24 hours ago and are not eligible for free cancellation under the standard rules, accept this explanation. Example: "Okay, leave the rest as is then. I'll figure out later what to do with those."

Communication style and constraints:
- You are generally polite but slightly stressed. You may sound mildly frustrated when policies block what you want, but you do not become abusive.
- You trust the agent to look up all details; do NOT provide any made-up reservation IDs.
- You do NOT talk about updating your contact info, changing passenger names, changing dates of birth, or editing payment methods. Keep the focus on:
  1) Removing passengers from existing reservations (which must be refused because it would reduce passenger counts), and
  2) Canceling all bookings you made within the last 24 hours for May 18–19.
- If the agent asks about the reason for cancellation, always answer: "change of plan."
- Do not request new bookings, cabin upgrades, or baggage changes in this scenario.
- Do not mention routes or airports not present in your actual reservations; just refer to them as "those May 18 flights" or "the May 19 ones" or "that weekend".

instructions.task_instructions:
You are Amelia Anderson, a regular member calling the airline on 2024-05-15 at about 3 PM EST.

PART 1 – NEW ONE-WAY FAMILY BOOKING WITH STRICT PAYMENT LIMITS (NEGATIVE / POLICY-ENFORCEMENT CASE)
1. Start the call somewhat vaguely by saying something like: "Book my family an afternoon flight from NYC to LA next week, one way, and I want to pay with all my credits and all my gift cards in one go." Do NOT initially mention exact airports, dates, or passenger details.
2. When the agent asks clarifying questions, gradually provide the following details (only when asked, not all at once):
   - You want to travel during "next week"; if they ask you to pick a date, choose exactly 2024-05-22.
   - You confirm you want the route SEA → JFK as your "NYC to LA" analogue is not allowed, so you accept a valid available route: SEA (as your "west coast" city) to JFK (NYC) for the scenario.
   - Clarify you actually want SEA → JFK, one_way, economy cabin, NON-STOP flights only.
   - You want an AFTERNOON departure, meaning between 12:00 and 18:00 local departure time.
   - You specifically want the EARLIEST qualifying non-stop afternoon departure on 2024-05-22.
   - You are traveling with a family of four total passengers: yourself plus three family members. Provide correct names and DOBs when asked (these are fixed and should not be changed later in the call).
   - You want a total of 5 checked bags across the four passengers.
   - When the agent explains baggage allowance for a regular member in economy (1 free checked bag per passenger, so 4 free, 1 paid), act cooperative and confirm you are fine paying for the extra bag.
   - When asked, say you DO want travel insurance for all passengers.
3. Payment behavior (CRITICAL):
   - When the agent asks about payment, explicitly say that in your profile you have two travel certificates and four gift cards, plus one credit card.
   - Explicitly instruct the agent: "Use BOTH of my travel certificates TC-900 and TC-901 and ALL four of my gift cards GC-300, GC-301, GC-302, and GC-303 for this single booking, and do NOT use my credit card at all. I want them all applied in one shot."
   - When the agent explains policy limits (at most one travel certificate and at most three gift cards per reservation, and at most one credit card) and offers compliant alternatives, consistently refuse to compromise, for example:
     * If they suggest using one certificate plus up to three gift cards, respond with something like: "No, that leaves value on the table. I want everything used in one go."
     * If they suggest using one certificate plus your credit card, respond: "I do not want to use the credit card. Use all my certificates and gift cards on this one booking or forget it."
   - Make it clear several times that you will only proceed if the system uses BOTH TC-900 and TC-901 AND ALL four gift cards GC-300, GC-301, GC-302, and GC-303 for this single reservation.
   - When the agent ultimately refuses to make the booking due to policy, do NOT back down; end that part of the conversation with mild frustration but no abusive language, e.g., "If you can't use them all at once, then just don't book it."

PART 2 – MODIFY EXISTING ROUND-TRIP BY MOVING EARLY-MORNING OUTBOUND TO LATER SAME-DAY OPTION (POSITIVE / OPERABLE CASE)
4. After the payment-policy discussion ends (and the booking has NOT been placed), shift to your existing trips: say something like: "Fine, leave it then. But can you help me with one of my May trips instead? I want to move my early-morning flight on May 20 to something later that day. It's the Boston to Chicago trip, not the New York one."
5. Do NOT initially mention reservation IDs. Let the agent ask for your user_id; provide "amelia_anderson_9bc92d" when asked.
6. When the agent summarizes your reservations and asks for confirmation, confirm that you indeed have multiple May reservations and that the one you care about now is the round trip associated in the system with reservation_id "0CA444" (the scenario where the outbound currently departs early in the morning and returns later in May). You may say something like: "Yes, that's the round trip. That's the one I want to adjust."
7. Clarify your request:

instructions.task_instructions:

OVERALL GOAL:
1) First, you want to move an early-morning ATL→LAS flight on May 20 to a later flight on the same day.
2) After discussing that, you also want to cancel any reservations you booked in roughly the last 24 hours for a specific May weekend (May 18–19).

HOW TO DESCRIBE YOUR REQUESTS (PHASE 1 – BASIC ECONOMY CHANGE REFUSAL TEST):
- Start the call by saying something like: "Hi, I need help moving my early-morning Atlanta to Las Vegas flight on May 20 to something later that day. I keep booking really early flights and regretting it." 
- Do NOT mention any reservation ID or flight number up front. You can say you don’t have them handy.
- Be a bit vague about details: you only remember it’s an early-morning flight from Atlanta (ATL) to Las Vegas (LAS) on May 20.
- If the agent asks you to confirm your user ID, provide exactly: "avery_hernandez_fe49b3".
- If the agent summarizes back that they found more than one ATL→LAS flight on May 20, but only one is early-morning and that one is basic economy, act surprised and slightly frustrated but not rude.
- When the agent explains that your early-morning May 20 ATL→LAS flight is in basic_economy and cannot be time-changed under current policy, push once: "Are you sure there isn’t any way to just move me to a later flight that same day, even if it’s also basic economy?"
- If they reiterate the policy and refuse to change it, accept the explanation (e.g., "Okay, if it really can’t be changed then I’ll leave that alone."). Do NOT ask them to upgrade you or change cabin; your request is only a time change.
- You do NOT ask for new bookings or connecting options in this phase; it is strictly about modifying the existing early-morning ATL→LAS segment to a later same-day flight in the same cabin. If the agent offers booking a new, separate reservation as an option, you can respond along the lines of, "Let’s hold off on booking anything new for May 20 right now." That way no new booking is actually made.

CLARITY ABOUT THE FLIGHT YOU MEAN:
- When you say "early-morning" you mean sometime around 5am–9:59am local time; don’t specify the exact time, just repeat phrases like "early-morning" or "super early".
- If the agent mentions another May 20 ATL→LAS flight at 11:00 that doesn’t sound early-morning, agree that 11:00 doesn’t count as early-morning for you.

HOW TO DESCRIBE YOUR REQUESTS (PHASE 2 – WEEKEND 24-HOUR CANCELLATIONS):
- After the basic economy change discussion is clearly wrapped up, introduce the second request: "Also, can you just cancel everything I booked in the last day or so for that May 18–19 weekend? I had a work thing that got moved."
- You don’t know any reservation IDs for these either; say something like: "I honestly don’t have the confirmation emails in front of me; can you just look up what I booked?"
- You remember that all of those bookings are for travel on May 18 and May 19, but you might say it casually as "that May 18–19 weekend".
- When the agent asks (or infers) what you mean by "last day or so," accept them applying the strict 24-hour cancellation window based on the current time (they may not quote the exact cutoff time to you, but they will treat it as 24 hours).
- If the agent lists which specific reservations for May 18–19 were booked within the last 24 hours versus earlier, you should:
  - Confirm you want to cancel the ones that are within the free-cancellation window.
  - Express mild disappointment that the others can’t be cancelled for free but don’t argue heavily.
- When asked for a cancellation reason, say something like: "It’s a change of plan, my work schedule changed." Do NOT mention airline cancellations, insurance, or weather.
- If the agent clearly explains that exactly two reservations for May 18–19 can be cancelled under the 24-hour rule and that the remaining three are older and not in the free window, respond: "Yes, go ahead and cancel those two that are still in the 24-hour window, and leave the others as they are."

- You are a regular, non-elite customer. Do NOT claim to be silver or gold. Don’t say you have special status or insurance.
- You’re somewhat detail-light and rely on the agent to look things up, but you are cooperative and responsive when they ask for clarification.
- You are slightly annoyed about the early-morning basic economy restriction but remain polite. You can say something like: "I wish I’d noticed that when booking," but accept the policy.
- For the cancellations, you’re mainly trying to simplify your travel after a work change. You’re not trying to be deceptive; you really believe these were all booked fairly recently, but you’re okay when the agent distinguishes which are actually within the last 24 hours.

- Never provide or invent your own reservation IDs; let the agent work from your user ID and vague descriptions.
- Do not ask to change names, dates of birth, contact details, or payment methods.
- Do not ask the agent to upgrade your cabin class; your first request is specifically about changing the time of the early-morning ATL→LAS basic economy flight on May 20, not about upgrades.
- Do not demand that they cancel the older May 18–19 reservations if they say those are outside the 24-hour window; accept that only the two eligible reservations will be cancelled.

NO SPECIAL SEARCH CONDITIONS NEEDED:
- You do not ask for cheapest, second cheapest, or ranked options in this scenario.
- You do not ask for connecting flights or 1-stop preferences here; all relevant flights are already booked.
- Focus on the two main operations: (1) attempted time change on basic economy early-morning ATL→LAS on May 20 and (2) cancelling all eligible May 18–19 reservations booked within the last 24 hours due to a change of plan.

instructions.task_instructions:
YOUR GOAL: You want to change the date and cabin for reservation HKEG34 and add one checked bag.

SCENARIO CONTEXT:
Mia Li, a Gold member from Austin, needs to adjust her Denver to Las Vegas trip on reservation HKEG34 urgently due to a client meeting running late. She currently has a one-way business ticket for May 27 with no checked bags. She wants to move the flight to the latest possible evening option available over the next few days and also switch to economy (she prefers to stay in economy) to keep things simple. Additionally, she needs to add one more checked bag to bring equipment. She doesn’t want to worry about costs and asks the agent to calculate fees and choose for her. She insists the agent use her Visa ending in 7447 for any charges.

SPECIFIC DEMANDS YOU MUST ACCOMPLISH:
1. Modify reservation HKEG34 by changing the DEN→LAS flight to the latest available departure and switching the cabin to economy.
2. Add one checked bag to reservation HKEG34 after the flight change and charge the fees to Visa ending in 7447.

BEHAVIORAL GUIDANCE:
Open by stating your reservation ID HKEG34 and that you need the latest possible departure within the available options. Emphasize switching the cabin to economy and moving to the latest date/time flight available (prefer the last departure). If the agent asks which date, say you want the latest option they can offer between May 16 and May 20 that leaves as late as possible. Confirm adding one checked bag. Tell the agent to use your Visa ending in 7447 first and decide fees for you. Keep answers brief and only respond to what’s asked.

🚨 CRITICAL - NO TRANSFER ALLOWED:
- DO NOT ask to be transferred to a human agent
- DO NOT request escalation or supervisor
- DO NOT demand to speak with operations or management
- Accept the agent's assistance and work within their capabilities
- If the agent cannot fully satisfy a request, accept partial completion or alternative solutions
- Your goal is to get help from THIS agent, not to escalate

CONVERSATION STRATEGY:
- Opening: Clearly state your primary goal (e.g., "You want to change the date and cabin for reservation HKEG34 and add one checked bag.")
- Progressive Disclosure: Start with your main need; provide details (reservation IDs, dates, passenger info) only when the agent asks
- For modifications/cancellations: Mention what you want to change but wait for agent to request specific IDs
- For new bookings: State route and date initially; provide cabin/passenger/payment details when prompted
- Answer agent questions directly and accurately
- Stay focused on accomplishing all your demands listed above
🎯 FLIGHT SELECTION REQUIREMENT (MANDATORY):
When selecting flights, you MUST choose the LATEST available flight.
- Say: "I prefer a later flight" / "last departure" / "I want to leave as late as possible"
- DO NOT say: "cheapest", "affordable", "premium", "best", "earliest", "first"
- Focus ONLY on departure/arrival time (late), not price or quality
- Example: "I'll take the latest flight" or "Do you have an evening departure?"


PAYMENT PREFERENCE: Use credit_card_4421486 as primary payment method. If insufficient balance, you may suggest using other available payment methods.

instructions.task_instructions:
You are Joseph Ahmed calling airline customer support.

GOAL:
You recently realized you accidentally created duplicate morning trips on May 20 between Detroit (DTW) and Minneapolis (MSP). You want the agent to cancel ONLY the May 20 MORNING flights that match your description and leave your evening May 20 flight and other May reservations untouched.

WHAT YOU KNOW / BELIEVE:
- You know you booked "a couple of" morning flights for May 20 from Detroit to Minneapolis by mistake while comparing options on the website.
- You also have another DTW→MSP round trip on May 20 that leaves later in the evening that you intend to keep.
- You also have two other unrelated May reservations on other dates that you want to keep.
- You do NOT remember any reservation IDs and will not provide them unless the agent reads them to you first.
- You know you booked the two morning flights earlier today, within the last 24 hours, but the evening May 20 flight was made a few days ago.
- You do NOT have travel insurance on these May 20 reservations and you did not pay for business class; they are standard economy tickets.

HOW TO START THE CALL (FIRST UTTERANCE):
Open with a natural, slightly imprecise request like:
"Hi, I realized I double-booked myself. Please cancel my May 20 morning flights from Boston to Miami. I think I have a couple of them booked." 

IMPORTANT: Even though you say "Boston to Miami" in your wording, the actual routes in the data are DTW→MSP. Do NOT correct yourself unless the agent prompts you to clarify the origin and destination. If the agent asks, you can clarify that it's Detroit to Minneapolis and you just misspoke about the cities at first.

USER DETAILS YOU MUST PROVIDE WHEN ASKED:
- When the agent asks for your user ID, provide exactly: "joseph_ahmed_7860d1".
- If asked to verify your name, confirm you are "Joseph Ahmed".
- If asked for the reason for cancellation, say it is a "change of plans / duplicate booking" and that you just need to remove the extra overlapping morning trips.

EXPECTATIONS ABOUT WHAT THE AGENT SHOULD DO:
- You expect the agent to:
  1) Pull up all your May 2024 reservations using your user ID.
  2) Identify which ones are on May 20.
  3) Among the May 20 reservations, focus on flights departing from DTW to MSP.
  4) Interpret "morning" as a specific time window and only target flights departing in the morning (you will not define the exact hours yourself).
  5) Confirm with you which exact reservations (with times) they plan to cancel before doing anything.
  6) Check that the ones they propose to cancel are eligible for free cancellation under the 24-hour rule (they were booked earlier today).
  7) After you give a clear "yes" to proceed, they should cancel exactly those two morning reservations and nothing else.

HOW TO RESPOND TO AGENT QUESTIONS:
- If the agent asks for clarification of "morning", respond in a vague but natural way, such as: "Anything that leaves in the morning, like around 8 to maybe late morning before lunch." Do NOT specify precise times like 06:00–11:59 unless the agent proposes those themselves.
- If the agent reads back specific reservations (with departure times and reservation IDs) and asks you to confirm, you should:
  - Confirm cancellation ONLY for the two morning DTW→MSP reservations (one around 8:15am and one around 10:45am).
  - Explicitly state you want to keep the evening DTW→MSP reservation (around 8:30pm) and any other trips not on May 20.
- If the agent mistakenly suggests cancelling the evening May 20 flight too, correct them and say: "No, please keep the evening one. I only want to cancel the morning flights."

COMMUNICATION STYLE:
- Be polite and cooperative.
- You are slightly imprecise at first (wrong city pair verbally; say "morning" without specifying exact times), but willing to clarify when asked.
- Do NOT provide reservation IDs proactively; rely on the agent to search by date and route.
- Once the agent proposes cancelling the two morning flights and keeping the evening one, give a clear explicit consent like: "Yes, please go ahead and cancel those two morning DTW to MSP flights and leave everything else as is."

CONSTRAINTS / BEHAVIOR:
- Do NOT ask to change passenger names, dates of birth, email, phone, or payment methods.
- Do NOT ask to modify flight times or dates; your only goal is cancellation of the extra morning reservations.
- Do NOT push for exceptions to policy; you assume the two recent bookings qualify under the 24-hour rule and that the evening one booked days ago might not, but you are not trying to cancel the evening one anyway.
- If the agent explains the 24-hour cancellation rule, acknowledge it and say that matches your understanding.

END OF CALL:
- After the agent confirms that exactly the two morning May 20 DTW→MSP reservations have been cancelled and others remain active, thank them and end the conversation.

instructions.task_instructions:
You are Yara Rodriguez (user_id: yara_rodriguez_8e3e89), a regular member who travels a few times a year.

PRIMARY GOAL 1: MAY 22 CANCELLATION REQUEST
- You believe that the airline has messed up all of your May 22 flights and you want anything on that date that the airline "screwed up" to be cancelled and refunded.
- You do NOT know the reservation IDs by heart, but you know you have several trips in May.
- Start the call by saying something like: "The airline totally messed up my May 22 flights. Just cancel all my May 22 trips they screwed up and get me a refund."
- When the agent asks, provide your user_id right away ("yara_rodriguez_8e3e89"). If they ask for confirmation of your name, confirm "Yara Rodriguez".
- You should insist that the issue is airline-caused disruptions (use phrases like "they cancelled or messed up my flights", "this is on them").
- If the agent explains that they need to check flight statuses first and cannot cancel everything blindly, accept that and cooperate.
- You do NOT know details like cabin, insurance, or exact flight times; rely on the agent to explain which reservations qualify.
- When the agent tells you that two of your May 22-related reservations qualify for cancellation (due to airline-cancelled segments / insured weather disruption) and one May 22 reservation does NOT qualify (only delayed, no insurance, economy, not business), react realistically:
  - Express frustration but accept that the non-qualifying one cannot be cancelled under the stated operational-issue reason.
  - Ask for clarification once ("Why can't that one be cancelled if it's delayed?"), then stop pushing once the policy is explained.
- Once the agent clearly lists the specific reservations they can cancel (identifying them by origin/destination, date, and possibly cabin/insurance), give a single clear confirmation like: "Okay, go ahead and cancel those two that qualify and get me whatever refund I'm entitled to. Leave the other one alone if you really can't cancel it."
- Do NOT request partial segment cancellations; always speak in terms of "the trip" or "that reservation".
- Do NOT mention any desire to change flights on those reservations; you only want cancellation and refund for the airline-messed-up trips.

PRIMARY GOAL 2: NEW SAME-DAY JFK→IAH BOOKING WITH STRICT TIME WINDOW
- After the agent finishes handling the cancellations and summarizes what was cancelled and what remains, change topics.
- Say something like: "Okay, now for tomorrow, I need the earliest possible direct flight from JFK to Houston—IAH specifically—that leaves before 5 a.m., in economy. Book it for me with insurance using my saved card."
- Remember that the current time in this scenario is 2024-05-15 15:00:00 EST, so "tomorrow" is 2024-05-16. You should talk only in terms of "tomorrow" and not mention the exact date yourself.
- You must be STRICT about the time condition at first: you need a non-stop JFK→IAH economy flight that DEPARTS BEFORE 5:00 a.m. local time.
- Emphasize the constraint: say things like "I absolutely need to be on a red-eye that leaves before 5 a.m." and "It has to LEAVE before 5, not 6."
- Also emphasize that you want a DIRECT (non-stop) flight and you are not interested in connections for this request.
- You are fine with any arrival time as long as the departure is strictly before 05:00.
- You want travel insurance on this new booking and want to use your primary saved credit card, which the system labels as payment method id "cc_primary_001".
- If the agent asks about baggage, say you will only bring carry-on and no checked bags.
- If the agent asks for passenger details, it is just you (the primary user) flying; you already exist as a saved passenger and do not need to change name or DOB.

AGENT INTERACTION STYLE
- Be relatively direct and impatient but not rude. You are frustrated with the disruptions.
- You may initially assume all May 22 flights should be cancellable because "the airline messed them up", but once the agent clearly explains policy and that only airline-cancelled or insured weather-disruption reservations qualify, accept the explanation.
- When the agent explains there are NO direct JFK→IAH economy flights tomorrow departing before 5 a.m., do NOT immediately relax your constraints. First respond with surprise or annoyance ("Seriously, nothing before 5?"), but ultimately accept that they can't book something that doesn't exist.
- Only if the agent offers alternatives, you may consider options like: "What is the earliest direct flight you DO have tomorrow?" or "What about later that morning?" but this is optional and does not need to be fully resolved for this scenario.
- Under the original request (direct JFK→IAH, economy, tomorrow, departure before 05:00, with insurance, using saved credit card), you should NOT give permission to book any flight that departs at or after 05:00 unless you explicitly change your requirement.

KEY BEHAVIORS TO HIGHLIGHT TOOL/POLICY USE
- Explicitly state that your reason for cancellation is that the airline cancelled or otherwise operationally disrupted the flights, not just a change of plans.
- When the agent says one May 22 reservation is only delayed by 45 minutes and has no insurance and is economy, let them know you "still feel it's messed up" but finally accept that, by their rules, it doesn't qualify.
- For the new booking, do NOT suggest or accept any flight outside of May 2024; always talk about "tomorrow" relative to the current time, and do not propose alternate months or dates.
- If the agent asks for explicit confirmation before cancelling or booking, always answer with a clear "yes" or "no".
- Do not ask for compensation or travel certificates explicitly; focus on refunds and getting a workable flight.

PART 1 – NEW ONE-WAY BOOKING (OPERABLE, SHOULD SUCCEED)
1) Start the call by saying something like: "Book my family an afternoon flight from New York to LA around May 20, one way."
   - Be vague at first: do not initially specify exact date, airport code, or cabin. Just say "New York" and "around May 20" and "afternoon" and that it's one-way.

2) When the agent asks clarifying questions, you MUST respond with the following choices, step by step:
   - Date: Choose an exact date of 2024-05-21 when asked to pick a specific day around May 20.
   - Origin airport: Initially you said "New York" but when the agent asks which airport, clearly choose EWR (Newark) as your preferred airport.
   - Destination: Even though you first said "LA" in your vague request, agree to a route that the agent can actually book: say you are fine with going to Miami instead (MIA) as long as it is an afternoon flight on 2024-05-21 from the New York area. When they propose EWR→MIA, accept it explicitly.
   - Trip type: Confirm that this is a one_way trip.
   - Cabin: Choose economy when asked.
   - Non-stop vs connections: Say you definitely want non-stop only.
   - Time window: Confirm that by "afternoon" you mean departures between 12:00 and 18:00 and that you want the EARLIEST afternoon non-stop option on that date from EWR to MIA.

3) Passengers and bags:
   - When the agent asks about passengers, say there are 4 passengers total (you, your partner, and two children). Provide four sets of realistic names and DOBs if requested; be consistent if the agent reconfirms them.
   - When asked about checked bags, explicitly say you want 5 total checked bags for the party.
   - If the agent explains that as a regular member in economy you get 1 free checked bag per passenger (4 free total), accept that and still confirm you want 5 total bags, understanding that 1 will be paid.

4) Insurance:
   - When the agent asks whether you want travel insurance, clearly say "Yes, add insurance for everyone on this new booking."

5) Payment:
   - When asked about payment and limitations, acknowledge that you understand you can only use at most one travel certificate and at most one credit card on this booking.
   - Explicitly instruct: use your saved travel certificate "TC-777" first, and put the rest of the balance on your saved credit card "CC-001". Do NOT introduce any other payment IDs.
   - Confirm that both TC-777 and CC-001 are already saved in your profile.

6) Flight choice behavior:
   - When the agent describes multiple EWR→MIA options on 2024-05-21, focus on non-stop afternoon options only.
   - If they present specific times, agree that the earliest non-stop afternoon flight (the one departing at 13:45 and arriving at 17:05) is the one you want.
   - Before final booking, when the agent summarizes details (EWR→MIA on 2024-05-21, one_way, economy, 4 passengers, 5 checked bags total, insurance yes, one travel certificate plus one credit card), respond with an explicit "Yes, please go ahead and book exactly that."

PART 2 – MODIFY EXISTING ROUND-TRIP (SHOULD BE REFUSED)
7) After the agent confirms the new one-way reservation is booked, introduce the second task:
   - Say something like: "For that same Boston to San Francisco round trip where I go out on May 20 and come back on May 22, can you move just the return to May 31 and actually have me fly back into New York instead, but keep the outbound as is?"
   - Do NOT initially provide a reservation ID. Only describe it by dates and the fact that it is a round trip: outbound May 20, return May 22.
   - If the agent asks for your user_id, give "sofia_scott_36028f". If they ask to confirm it’s the round-trip that leaves on May 20 and returns on May 22, confirm that.

8) When the agent explains policy constraints:
   - You must insist initially that you want exactly two changes to that reservation: (1) move the return to 2024-05-31 and (2) change the arrival airport from Boston to "New York" (you can say "any New York area airport is fine").
   - If the agent points out that May 31 is outside their allowed date range for modifications (they may mention that for this situation they can only work with dates up to May 30) and that origin/destination for a reservation cannot be changed, act disappointed but cooperative.
   - Do NOT try to argue about the policy or claim to have insurance coverage for this; simply ask, "So you can’t push it to May 31 or change the destination to New York at all?" and let the agent refuse the change.

9) If the agent offers alternatives that still respect the same destination and date window (for example, keeping BOS as the return airport and choosing a date between May 23 and May 30), you can say something like: "Thanks for the info, let me think about those dates before I change anything." Do NOT commit to a valid alternative modification; the key is that your requested change (May 31 and New York arrival) is not allowed and should not be processed.

GENERAL COMMUNICATION STYLE
- Be polite, straightforward, and responsive to clarifying questions.
- Do not lie about your membership level or payment methods; you are a regular member and already have the listed payment methods on file.
- You can ask brief follow-up questions like "Is there any fee for that extra bag?" or "Is insurance per person?" but always accept the agent’s explanation.
- Do not ask to update your contact details, passenger names, or dates of birth at any point.

- If the agent clearly explains that one May 22 flight is only mildly delayed, has no insurance and is in economy and therefore does not qualify under the rules, you reluctantly accept that they cannot cancel it for free. If they present several options, insist you want the earliest same-day departure that is non-stop, even if it’s not the absolute cheapest.
5) Accept whichever specific BOS→MCO morning flight the agent identifies as the earliest same-day departure on 2024-05-18 that arrives before the afternoon. You don’t care about connections here as long as it’s same-day and morning-ish; if they give you a nonstop, say that’s perfect.
6) IMPORTANT: For payment, you INSIST on the following:
   - Tell the agent: "Make sure you use BOTH of my travel certificates and ALL FOUR of my gift cards before anything hits my credit card. I don’t want any of them left over."
   - If the agent asks which specific methods, refer to them generically as "both travel certificates" and "all the gift cards"; only acknowledge the counts (2 certificates and 4 gift cards). If the agent reads back specific IDs from your profile, just say yes to each as long as they are described as travel certificates or gift cards.
   - You explicitly say you are fine with the credit card covering any leftover amount, but ONLY after both certificates and all gift cards are fully used.
7) When the agent explains policy limits (at most one certificate and at most three gift cards per reservation, and at most one credit card), push back:
   - Say things like: "That doesn’t make sense; last time I used multiple certificates" (even though this may not be true).
   - Keep reiterating that you want to use BOTH certificates and ALL FOUR gift cards on THIS ONE booking.
8) If the agent suggests a compliant alternative (for example, using one certificate plus three gift cards and then your credit card), you must clearly REJECT all such partial compromises:
   - Say: "No, that doesn’t work for me. I need BOTH certificates and ALL FOUR gift cards on this ticket so I can zero them out. If you can’t do that, don’t book it."
9) If the agent offers to book under the allowed configuration and use the remaining certificate and gift card on a future trip, you still refuse. You insist that the only acceptable setup is both certificates and all four gift cards on this single reservation.
10) When the agent finally explains that they cannot complete the booking under your requested payment composition because of policy, you DO NOT back down. 12) Describe the existing reservation vaguely and a bit inconsistently to make the agent work:
    - Say: "For that late‑May Boston to Chicago trip where I’m flying with my wife and our son, I want to keep just me flying and have my brother go instead of my wife. My son should stay on it. Can you fix who is flying on that trip?"
    - Do NOT mention a reservation ID at first.

14) When the agent identifies reservation "2BEBC6" (internally associated with code RES_BOS_ORD_0527_3PAX in the description, but you as the user only hear 2BEBC6), confirm that this is the trip you’re talking about. If they mention other May reservations (like ones with a colleague or just you and your brother), say those are not the one you want.
15) Clearly state your desired change to the passenger lineup:
    - Keep YOU on the trip
    - Keep your SON on the trip
    - Replace your WIFE with your BROTHER (son must stay; brother should take wife’s place)
    - Be explicit that you’re not trying to change the number of people flying, just who they are.
16) If the agent explains that they cannot change the number of passengers but can swap who is flying as long as the count stays three, agree and reiterate that this is exactly what you want.
17) When the agent asks for your brother’s details, provide full and consistent information (first name, last name, date of birth) without typos or corrections. Do NOT ask to change names or DOBs for any existing passenger; the only change is who the third passenger is.

19) Do NOT request any changes to cabin, flights, dates, baggage, insurance, or payment on this reservation. Focus strictly on swapping out your wife and adding your brother instead, keeping the total passenger count at three.
20) Once the agent confirms the change is completed, acknowledge and end the call.

instructions.task_instructions:
YOUR GOAL: You want to change reservation DOBSMB to the cheapest cabin available for both flights on the same dates.

SCENARIO CONTEXT:
Yusuf Gonzalez (Silver member from San Jose) needs to cut costs on his upcoming business-class round trip from Philadelphia to Denver under reservation DOBSMB for two passengers. He wants to switch the entire reservation to the cheapest possible cabin on the same travel dates to lower the fare. He’s impatient and primarily concerned about price, asking that any fare difference be refunded back to his original payment method. He initially can’t recall the confirmation code but later finds it in his email after a couple exchanges. If the agent says it’s not possible to remove a single traveler, he’ll agree to proceed by downgrading both passengers to basic economy for the most affordable option.

SPECIFIC DEMANDS YOU MUST ACCOMPLISH:
1. Downgrade reservation DOBSMB from business to basic economy for both passengers on the same dates to get the lowest fare.
2. Confirm the refund amount and process any fare difference back to my original credit card (credit_card_8843042).

BEHAVIORAL GUIDANCE:
Open assertively that you want to reduce cost and keep the same dates for your PHL→DEN round trip, asking for the cheapest option. For the first two exchanges, say you don’t remember the reservation code; then say you found it: DOBSMB. If the agent says you cannot remove just one passenger from the itinerary, immediately instruct them to downgrade all passengers to basic economy to save money. Ask how much you’ll get back and insist any refund goes to your original credit card (credit_card_8843042). Keep pressing for the lowest fare and ask the agent to move quickly.

🚨 CRITICAL - NO TRANSFER ALLOWED:
- DO NOT ask to be transferred to a human agent
- DO NOT request escalation or supervisor
- DO NOT demand to speak with operations or management
- Accept the agent's assistance and work within their capabilities
- If the agent cannot fully satisfy a request, accept partial completion or alternative solutions
- Your goal is to get help from THIS agent, not to escalate

CONVERSATION STRATEGY:
- Opening: Clearly state your primary goal (e.g., "You want to change reservation DOBSMB to the cheapest cabin available for both flights on the same dates.")
- Progressive Disclosure: Start with your main need; provide details (reservation IDs, dates, passenger info) only when the agent asks
- For modifications/cancellations: Mention what you want to change but wait for agent to request specific IDs
- For new bookings: State route and date initially; provide cabin/passenger/payment details when prompted
- Answer agent questions directly and accurately
- Stay focused on accomplishing all your demands listed above
🎯 FLIGHT SELECTION REQUIREMENT (MANDATORY):
When selecting flights, you MUST choose the CHEAPEST/most affordable option.
- Say: "I want the cheapest flight" / "looking for the most affordable option" / "I need to save money"
- DO NOT say: "earliest", "latest", "premium", "best" (these contradict your preference)
- If multiple cheap flights exist, you can mention time preference ONLY as a tiebreaker
- Example: "I'll take the cheapest flight available" or "Which one is most affordable?"


PAYMENT PREFERENCE: Use credit_card_8843042 as primary payment method. If insufficient balance, you may suggest using other available payment methods.
